relationship.statement: A pendulum's swing period grows as the square root of string length and shrinks with stronger gravity, while bob mass cancels out. Release angle sets swing width and peak speed, and slightly lengthens the period once swings are no longer small.
assumptions: Air drag, pivot friction, and string mass are neglected.
The pendulum bob acts as a point mass on a taut, inextensible line.
Small swing angles (sin θ ≈ θ) are assumed for the simple period law.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the fixed pivot point to the bob's center of mass.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration pulling the bob toward equilibrium.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the pendulum bob; increases weight and inertia equally.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle measured from straight down where the bob is released.

quantities.label: Swing period
quantities.meaning: Exact time for one complete back-and-forth swing at any release angle.

quantities.label: Small-angle period
quantities.meaning: Ideal period 2π√(L/g) when sin θ ≈ θ, ignoring release angle.

quantities.label: Peak speed
quantities.meaning: Speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest vertical point.

quantities.label: Restoring force
quantities.meaning: Tangential force m·g·sin(θ₀) pulling the bob back at release.

quantities.label: Restoring accel.
quantities.meaning: Tangential acceleration g·sin(θ₀) at release; bob mass cancels out.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { const L = inputs.length; const g = inputs.gravity; const deg = inputs.start_angle; const mass = 2; const theta0 = deg * Math.PI / 180; const omega0 = Math.sqrt(g / L); const small_angle_period = 2 * Math.PI / omega0; const k = Math.sin(0.5 * theta0); const kp = Math.cos(0.5 * theta0); let a = 1; let b = kp; const aArr = [1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]; const cArr = [k, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]; for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { const nextA = 0.5 * (a + b); const nextB = Math.sqrt(a * b); cArr[i] = 0.5 * (a - b); aArr[i] = nextA; a = nextA; b = nextB; } const period = small_angle_period / aArr[5]; const K = 0.5 * Math.PI / aArr[5]; const w = K - omega0 * t; let phi = 32 * aArr[5] * w; for (let i = 5; i >= 1; i--) { phi = 0.5 * (phi + Math.asin((cArr[i] / aArr[i]) * Math.sin(phi))); } const theta = 2 * Math.asin(k * Math.sin(phi)); const ideal_theta = theta0 * Math.cos(omega0 * t); const bob_x = L * Math.sin(theta); const bob_y = -L * Math.cos(theta); const ideal_x = L * Math.sin(ideal_theta); const ideal_y = -L * Math.cos(ideal_theta); const release_x = L * Math.sin(theta0); const release_y = -L * Math.cos(theta0); const max_speed = Math.sqrt(2 * g * L * (1 - Math.cos(theta0))); const restoring_accel = g * Math.sin(theta0); const restoring_force = mass * restoring_accel; const forceLen = 0.018 * restoring_force; const force_tip_x = release_x - forceLen * Math.cos(theta0); const force_tip_y = release_y - forceLen * Math.sin(theta0); const angle_deg = theta * 180 / Math.PI; const ideal_angle_deg = ideal_theta * 180 / Math.PI; return { period: period, small_angle_period: small_angle_period, max_speed: max_speed, restoring_force: restoring_force, restoring_accel: restoring_accel, angle_deg: angle_deg, ideal_angle_deg: ideal_angle_deg, bob_x: bob_x, bob_y: bob_y, ideal_x: ideal_x, ideal_y: ideal_y, release_x: release_x, release_y: release_y, force_tip_x: force_tip_x, force_tip_y: force_tip_y, neg_length: -L, is_small_angle: deg <= 20, is_large_angle: deg >= 55, is_fast_swing: period < 1.7, is_slow_swing: period > 3.2 }; }

always: Mass 2 kg cancels out of period.
Longer L and weaker g lengthen T.

cases.text: Small angle: simple T law holds.
Wide swing: exact bob lags ideal.
Short L or strong g: rapid swings.
Long L or weak g: slow swings.

lesson.title: What Changes a Pendulum's Swing?
lesson.description: Compare an exact pendulum against the small-angle law as you vary string length, gravity, and release angle. Watch how period, peak speed, and phase lag respond.
lesson.instructions: Adjust string length and gravity to see both bobs speed up or slow down while keeping bob mass fixed at 2 kg. Sweep release angle from 10 to 80 degrees to compare the true swing against the small-angle curve and watch the restoring force arrow F0 at release.
lesson.goal: Period scales as √(L/g), independent of bob mass, while wider release angles increase swing width, peak speed, and slightly lengthen the exact period beyond the small-angle law.
